errors.english: Should not be despised in this world,
errors.why: The verse says the person should do what is not reproached in this world and brings happiness hereafter; 'not reproached' qualifies the action, not the person.

errors.english: act like gurus or like a master—
errors.why: The sentence (continued on the next side) says one should regard others as one's elders or lords and not disparage them, not that the king should act like a guru.

note: A sound rendering of the buffalo-sacrifice and butcher's-son illustrations; only the verse's syntax and the final clause are slightly off.

errors.english: It refers to seeing however many things there are that are being excluded [note: original: བསལ་བ་, Sanskrit: apoha; the theory that words function by excluding what they are not].
errors.why: བསལ་བ here stands for གསལ་བ (individual instances, vyakti), as the lemma and the next side show; apoha is not at issue.

fix.find: It refers to seeing however many things there are that are being excluded [note: original: བསལ་བ་, Sanskrit: apoha; the theory that words function by excluding what they are not].
fix.replace: It refers to seeing however many individual instances there are [note: བསལ་བ་ read as གསལ་བ་, vyakti].

errors.english: introduces the Sāṃkhya [note: original: གྲངས་ཅན་, a school of Hindu philosophy] position, namely, the nature of color and so forth
errors.why: In this lemma gloss གྲངས་ཅན refers to the enumeration (color and the rest) that 'and so forth' brings in; no Sāṃkhya position is being introduced.

errors.english: [note: original: རྗེས་སུ་འགྲོ་བ་, Sanskrit: anvaya; the presence of a property in similar cases]
errors.why: Here རྗེས་སུ་འགྲོ་བ is the universal's running through its instances (anugama/anuvṛtti), not the logical anvaya of inference.

note: The lemma-by-lemma structure is followed, but two notes import doctrines (Sāṃkhya, apoha) that are not in the passage.
Accurate rendering of the argument on unobstructed capacity, non-perception and the Mīmāṃsaka objection.

errors.english: "You and the cowherd will come to know it through Śiva
errors.why: The phrase concerns the cowherd's woman (མ) named Śivā, whose hand throws the curd pot; it is not the god Śiva and 'the cowherd' is not a separate party here.
ཚང here is 'nest/lair', glossed on the next side as a dwelling place, not 'complete'.

note: A faithful run of word-glosses; only the obscure Śivā episode and the last lemma are misread.
Follows the apoha argument and the discussion of isolated words correctly; the doubled inline glosses are untidy but not wrong.

errors.english: If mind [note: original: སེམས་, citta] were the self [note: original: བདག་, ātman], it could not be the object of the view of self.
errors.why: The text states that the (past and future) mind is not the object of the view of self; there is no counterfactual 'if mind were the self'.

note: Good rendering of the three-times argument and the plantain-tree conclusion; the opening sentence is recast as a conditional.

errors.english: If that [note: distinction of consciousness] were without a cause
errors.why: 'That' is the (absent) distinction of transformation; the consequence is that consciousness too (ཀྱང) would be causeless, so the referent is not the distinction of consciousness.

errors.english: if there is a distinction in the cause of existence
errors.why: ཇི་ལྟར་སྲིད་པ means 'to whatever extent there is', i.e. insofar as the cause is distinguished; it is not 'the cause of existence (bhava)'.

note: The anti-materialist argument with the milk example is rendered soundly, with two small misreadings.

errors.english: Not understanding the intention of others, externalists and so forth have spoken. "Externalists from the generality" refers to the individual characteristics themselves.
errors.why: Because others might not grasp the intention, the root text says 'the external ones' etc.; 'external' means the particulars external to the universal, not non-Buddhist 'externalists' who speak.

fix.find: Not understanding the intention of others, externalists and so forth have spoken. "Externalists from the generality" refers to the individual characteristics themselves.
fix.replace: Because others might not understand the intention, he says "the external ones" and so forth. "External" to the universal means the individual characteristics themselves.

errors.english: when it perceives an appearance in what is called the (essential mind) tattva-buddhi,
errors.why: དེ་ཁོ་ན་ཞེས་བྱ་བ is a lemma ('that very'); the sentence says the conceptual cognition, grasping what appears to cognition, appears as if grasping a real thing; there is no 'tattva-buddhi'.

fix.find: when it perceives an appearance in what is called the (essential mind) tattva-buddhi,
fix.replace: when it grasps what appears to the cognition (on the words "that very"),

errors.english: Because of the power of intense attachment
errors.why: ལྷག་པར་ཞེན་པ is adhyavasāya, conceptual determination, a technical pramāṇa term, not emotional attachment.

errors.english: the commentators and others offer a reply
errors.why: The reply is given by the root passage beginning 'those who explain'; it is a lemma, not commentators replying.

note: The svalakṣaṇa/sāmānya discussion is broadly followed, but lemmas are mistaken for agents and adhyavasāya is mistranslated.
Faithful rendering of the general and specific, figurative and direct characteristics of the four truths.

errors.english: the head of (Indra) the king of the gods, here used in a logical syllogism
errors.why: བརྒྱ་བྱིན་གྱི་སྤྱི་བོ is śakramūrdhan, the anthill from which smoke-like vapour rises in the Pramāṇavārttika fire/smoke discussion, not literally Indra's head.

fix.find: the head of (Indra) the king of the gods, here used in a logical syllogism

errors.english: This is addressed by the statement:
errors.why: The root text states this very objection ('this is what is said by...'); it does not answer it.

note: The fire/smoke causation argument is mostly tracked, but the anthill example is misunderstood and the objection/reply structure blurs at the end.
